Sorry for the slow reply! I'm not sure of a commit on Mathlib master that's a good example, but if we change some of the tactic analysis linters to give TryThis suggestions, maybe this is a good data point?

For CI logisitcs, at least for the weekly linting, I was imagining when that workflow runs that it would open up a PR. There's occasionally some manual intervention that is preferable in my experience, so I wouldn't automate it completely.

And @Kim Morrison, you do want it completely automated, so that it just makes a commit to your branch/PR, right?
I think 90% of the win here is having a single command to run that applies the changes, and having it run in CI is the final 10% of the win

For those who'd like to try out an experimental version: :)

  1. add the following to your lakefile:
require "skimmer" from git "https://github.com/thorimur/skimmer" @ "v0.0.1+try-this"

then run lake update skimmer to update the manifest

  1. run lake build <tgt>:applyCurrentTryThis

    • <tgt> can be a package, library, or module, e.g. lake build Mathlib:applyCurrentTryThis (where it will be interpreted as a library)

  2. git add/commit the changes (currently this step is manual)

And that's it. :)

Notes:

  • Adding skimmer to the lakefile invalidates the cache. If you'd like a cache, you'll need to wait for CI after modifying the lakefile. (Note: it would be great to have a way to include skimmer in mathlib as a sort of dev dependency. I'm trying to find a better approach than "temporarily edit the lakefile".)
  • If you want to build locally, running lake build <tgt>:applyCurrentTryThis will also build all the modules necessary for <tgt> first; you don't need a separate lake build if things aren't built.
  • It will only apply the current suggestions, not suggestions caused by accepting earlier suggestions. (The infrastructure is available for the latter (on another branch), but it's slower. Let me know if you need this.)

I'm sure there will be unexpected behavior; please tell me about any errors/suboptimal behavior here! Or even just preferred workflows. All feedback is much appreciated.

I'll emphasize again that this is very much a work in progress which will evolve in both syntax and behavior soon. Please try it, but also don't include skimmer in your lakefile permanently or embed it in any automation just yet. I'm working with @Bryan Gin-ge Chen on the automation front, and that's up next in a little while. :)

In the meantime, if you'd like to experiment with it, hopefully it helps a bit, and let me know how you'd like to see it develop! :)
(Thanks also to @Sebastian Ullrich and @Mac Malone for assisting with a tricky bug in office hours just now that was blocking this :) )

#36712 adds a script scripts/runSkimmer.sh for Mathlib which attempts to get around the cache issue by having a "side package" in /scripts. It should be the case that you can run lake exe cache get && ./scripts/runSkimmer.sh and get a relatively fast application of all try this suggestions across mathlib. It does this by using a local require.

This script can be copy-pasted to other projects, the script's config variables (in source) adjusted, and then (with the new script) runSkimmer.sh --init can be run to set up the side package. But: lake seems to put dependencies of the local project in the side project's .lake file. Adjusting the side package's packagesDir to point to the top level .lake doesn't seem to work. So it may duplicate the full cache of mathlib inside the side project's .lake...I've only tried it on mathlib so far.
#36712 in the hands of bors :tada:
